scope: Each sparse Ising bond is determined by an unordered pair of different sites. Three signed literal-copy bonds and three triangle bonds have distinct masks even when source variables or signed literals repeat.
In the unrestricted two-body gadget each NAE clause gives exactly six occupied spin pairs; the Hamiltonian coefficients reproduce the signs in the executable edge table.
For the classical energy in Eq. (10), a signed two-site Walsh character contributes −1 exactly when the endpoint spins obey the sign on that bond. A negated literal may be handled by a spin flip.

Direct truth-table verification for a new signed Ising gadget. Three copy edges and an antiferromagnetic triangle have joint energy at least −4. Equality requires exact literal copies and a not-all-equal clause.

For m not-all-equal clauses, the unrestricted signed two-body glass energy is the sum of the explicit clause scores; the threshold −4m is attainable exactly for satisfiable formulas. This supplies a direct satisfiability source for the energy decision in Eqs. (10)–(11).

Each ordinary 3-CNF clause becomes two not-all-equal clauses sharing an auxiliary bit. A common anchor permits simultaneous spin inversion. Truth-table soundness and completeness give equivalence for empty formulas, repeated variables and negated literals.
For an ordinary 3-CNF on n variables with m clauses the unrestricted signed spin model has n+7m+1 sites and exactly 12m unit-strength bonds. Satisfiability is equivalent to attaining energy −8m.

A single signed quantum thermal-energy estimate at β=13N and relative root-mean-square precision 1/(24N) decides ordinary 3-SAT with failure probability at most 1/4 on the linear-size unrestricted two-body gadget. Its sign-free counterpart at this query is estimated by −12m.

A nearest-neighbour six-cycle with three negative bonds has minimum energy −4. At this energy the three terminals are not all equal; setting all three return spins to the third terminal realizes −4 for each legal terminal triple. A single copy bond has minimum −1.
The sum of all nonnegative wire and cycle energy defects vanishes exactly when every wire is satisfied and every clause cycle is at its local minimum.

At the compiled threshold each variable row and each private occurrence column carries a constant assignment. Its signed vertical contact makes the front terminal equal to the corresponding signed literal.
A source assignment prescribes the base row spins, the occurrence-column spins and the three return spins of each clause. These formulas construct a lattice witness for every satisfying assignment.

A new routing proof supplies the three-dimensional nearest-neighbour spin-glass decision premise of Troyer–Wiese Eq. (10). An NAE formula is satisfiable exactly when its three-layer copy rows, occurrence columns and frustrated six-cycles reach the compiled energy threshold.
Occurrence column numbers are unique. Copy rows, vertical contacts, column segments and the six rim slots at each clause occupy distinct positively oriented lattice positions.
Every generated endpoint belongs to the finite box of dimensions (3m+1) by (n+1) by 3. The existing cubicGlass forward-coordinate operation takes the unit axis step to that encoded endpoint.

Strictly positive axis steps have different endpoints and cannot reverse one another. Their unordered spin-flip masks uniquely identify the physical bond and satisfy the open-boundary cubic model’s self-edge test.
The occupied masks of the existing cubicGlass representation equal the emitted edge masks, including their signs. Each compiled edge contributes exactly once to the occupied bond count.

Term-by-term agreement between finite cubicGlass energy and the routed lattice energy proves the bidirectional reduction from NAE satisfiability to the threshold for an actual three-layer nearest-neighbour Hamiltonian with couplings 0, ±1.

Sequential XOR spin flips realize a configuration path whose endpoint is the cumulative flip and whose unscaled series-expansion weight is the product of the corresponding signed model couplings, as in Eqs. (4)–(6).
The mask on two distinct sites is their Boolean parity vector. Following six edges around a clause cycle flips each site twice and returns to the aligned configuration.

For every compiled NAE clause, its six-edge closed path has weight −1 in the signed quantum model and +1 in the comparison ferromagnet. This witnesses the actual sign problem on the constructed hardness instances.

Every source variable occurs in the finite name table. The executable first-match search returns its list index and counts at most the list length in equality comparisons. Array materialization preserves the literal table.

Dense occurrence-based renaming preserves satisfiability for arbitrary natural variable labels, including duplicates and unused numeric ranges. Constructing the table uses at most (3m)² equality comparisons on variable labels. This counts label comparisons; binary labels may span multiple bits.

The executable sparse compiler enumerates all wire and rim edge identifiers, emits their signed nearest-neighbour positions and agrees with the cubic coupling table. Its output length is exactly the number of occupied bonds.

Counting the emitted sparse records gives both the classical threshold (minus the bond count plus twice the NAE clause count) and a deterministic sign-free thermal-energy estimate at β=13N with relative error ≤1/(24N). The emitted length is at most 3N.

For m source 3-CNF clauses, the three-layer box contains exactly 72m²+48m+6 spin sites. Substituting its size, β=13N and inverse precision 24N in Eq. (9) yields an explicit polynomial bound for the signed oracle call.

End-to-end nearest-neighbour reduction from ordinary 3-SAT with arbitrary natural variable names. One integrable estimate having the stated relative mean-square bound decides satisfiability with error ≤1/4 using the emitted bond count as its threshold offset. At precisely that query the sign-free estimator is deterministic. Every nonempty instance also has a closed negative-weight path. An all-temperature sign-free sampling theorem and machine-level NP-to-BPP composition are outside this result.
